findings.text: Routine decides whether shadows for a guest frame may enter unsync state. Tracked frames are refused, frames eligible for large mapping succeed without work, synchronizing callers with remaining shadows are refused, prefetch needing a transition reports conflict, otherwise eligible smallest level shadows are flagged and ordering is enforced before later writable publication.

Only smallest granularity shadows may become unsync. Upper level shadows remain write guarded through tracking, so a frame that permits large mapping and lacks tracking cannot own a shadow. Flagged pages are expected to be smallest level.

Marking uses dedicated unsync guard mmu_unsync_pages_lock because some faults run under shared MMU lock where the logic is unsafe alone. Taker rechecks flag after acquiring guard to handle races. Clearing demands exclusive MMU lock, so set to clear cannot be missed while holding shared or exclusive lock.

Publishing writability before flag visibility would let a peer walk observe writability, miss the flag during lockless root scan after a flush, then use stale translation. A write barrier after marking pairs with a read barrier in root checking to close that window.

Write tracking query returns negative for missing slot or disabled tracking, positive when current slot array marks the frame, and with two address spaces also checks sibling space slot for the same frame before reporting negative.
Per slot tracking is a frame indexed array at smallest granularity read with single load semantics. Missing slot is treated as untracked and nonzero entry means tracked.

Leaf install distinguishes prior states. Prefetch with same backing and present leaf is spurious. Table pointer overwritten by large mapping unlinks its child. Changed backing drops old entry. Backing without slot builds MMIO entry and asks for emulation. Otherwise it constructs new entry, publishes on change, flushes remote entries on structural change, then records reverse mapping for new entries or refreshes access hints for retained ones. Write faults against guarded construction report write protected.

Writability construction tries to unsync reachable shadows for newly writable entries, skipping that work when overwriting an already writable leaf at same level because relevant shadows must already be unsync and backing is stable until zap. Failure forces write guarded entry and informs caller. Prefetch without synchronizing adds access tracking mark. Dirty slot marking follows access tracking adjustment and expects smallest level.

Entry bits start from present base plus shadow present and conditional accessed hint, strip execution under huge NX mitigation, translate guest read user and execution rights through shadow masks, set large size above smallest level, fold memory type host writability and encryption, place backing number, then validate against reserved and type execution tables and record host MMIO use for buffer clearing when needed.

Backing classification caches host MMIO outcome per construction using negative sentinel for unknown. Valid backing is MMIO only when reserved and nonzero and immune from UC MTRR under PAT, excluding DAX like cached pages. Invalid backing is MMIO when its host range has no RAM type in firmware map.

Host MMIO use sets a sticky flag on current shadow root when one exists else on global arch state, then requests all CPUs to leave guest mode. Later query returns root flag when rooted else global flag.

Reserved validation combines overlap with a format mask selected by bit seven and level, plus a type execution check that folds user executable into executable and indexes a bad combination table by low six bits.
Slot absence and signal pending are each recognized by equality with dedicated backing sentinels. Signal handling records interrupt exit reason and increments the signal exit counter.

Prefetch installer rejects counts beyond fixed window, resolves slot in dirty aware mode for write access, gathers contiguous host pages with writable fast lookup, installs each entry as prefetch with writable host view, then marks each page dirty to ensure writeback after possible guest store.
Dirty release tolerates null, marks dirty only for access tracked pages, then releases clean reference.

Direct prefetch runs only for direct smallest level shadows with access tracking and outside invalidation. It scans an aligned window around the fault entry, skips present entries and the fault entry itself, coalesces maximal runs of absent entries, and installs each run with parent access rights and frame derived from parent.
Order to level mapping caps huge support at largest level, warns on unexpected orders, and chooses largest fitting level among large, medium, else smallest.

Huge adjustment forces smallest handling for execution under NX workaround, smallest max, error or noslot backing, and dirty tracked slots. Otherwise it queries max mapping level, stores requested and goal levels, and aligns backing to goal boundary while asserting guest and backing alignment.

Downgrade step applies when desired large level already has a small entry whose child is marked NX disallowed. It restores next level address bits into backing and decrements goal so the walker descends one more level.

Direct walker adjusts huge goal, iterates shadow levels, applies NX downgrade per level, computes per level base frame, stops at goal, creates or reuses and links child tables, accounts NX huge state when disallowed, installs leaf, treats spurious as benign, otherwise prefetches around leaf. Mismatched goal is treated as fault.

Error backing dispatch maps signal pending to interrupt exit plus interrupted return, read only fault to emulation without caching, hardware poison to user bus signal plus retry, and all else to generic fault.

Missing slot handling clears guest address for TDP, diverts private faults to memory fault exit, caches MMIO info with masked access, initializes noslot backing as nonwritable, emulates immediately when MMIO caching is disabled or frame exceeds host maximum, otherwise continues toward MMIO entry install.

Observed fault descriptor carries slot, frame, backing, address, and flags for write, prefetch, writability, privacy and TDP mode, plus level fields for max, requested and goal, huge disallow flags, execution flag and NX workaround enable.

Observed shadow page carries unsync flag, role with level direct access and disable bits, table base, NX disallow flag, and sticky host MMIO flag. Observed slot carries address space id, base frame and dirty tracking state.
